macro_bullets: Nvidia's 31% surge on Jensen Huang's return to CEO reignited the AI trade, sending the Nasdaq sharply higher.
Fed's John Williams signaled interest rates will likely head higher 'over time' to address inflation.
Hedge funds posted their worst week since April 2025, sparking a defensive shift across portfolios.
Euro zone growth held steady in PMI data, though a deepening downturn in France clouded the outlook.
Iran vowed to use all its tools to confront a threatened US naval blockade, keeping geopolitical risk elevated.
internals_narrative: Risk-on rotation into chips dominated, with Semiconductors (+13.8%) and Robotics & Hardware (+15.6%) leading as NVDA (+31.5%), IREN, MU and MRVL surged double digits, while Energy (-0.8%) and Consumer Staples (-0.5%) lagged on losses in COP, XOM, STZ and KR.

ticker_notes.NVDA: Nvidia jumped 31% on Jensen Huang's return as CEO, driving a broad AI-trade rebound.
ticker_notes.IREN: IREN and other neocloud names were flagged as oversold amid AI-bubble fears.
ticker_notes.MU: Huang's return added an estimated $500 billion to Micron and other Nvidia-dependent AI stocks.
ticker_notes.DRAM: Semiconductor ETFs rebounded as analysts called the prior indiscriminate chip selling overdone.
ticker_notes.MRVL: Marvell rode the Nvidia-led tech surge that added $2 trillion to the Nasdaq 100.
ticker_notes.INTC: Intel rallied with the broad semiconductor rebound.
ticker_notes.SNDK: Sandisk slid even as one analysis argued it still looks below fair value after a 179% run.
ticker_notes.ELV: Proposed Medicare Advantage rating changes threaten $107 billion in payments, pressuring managed-care names.
ticker_notes.COP: ConocoPhillips struck a $4.4 billion North Sea deal, set to exit Norway after 50 years.
ticker_notes.STZ: Constellation Brands fell as defensive consumer stocks lost their luster.
ticker_notes.AMT: American Tower announced a proposed DISH/EchoStar litigation settlement involving a $525 million cash payment.
ticker_notes.MPC: Marathon Petroleum eased with energy, though strong crack spreads were cited as a cash-flow tailwind.
ticker_notes.OXY: Occidental declined alongside a broad pullback in energy stocks.
ticker_notes.AZO: AutoZone drew attention on what could lift the stock after a losing year.
ticker_notes.AIG: The FT drew 'uncanny' parallels between Nvidia and AIG as a cautionary signal.
ticker_notes.BA: Boeing popped, with expanding airborne electronic-warfare spending cited as a driver.
ticker_notes.AEP: American Electric Power gains as utility spending plans grow with large new power customers signing on.
